en: Two, and humans will have a huge role in that transformation, and you will have a huge role in that transformation.
zh: 第二，人类将在这种变革中发挥巨大作用，而你将在这场变革中发挥巨大作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And three, if we don't do this well, then like all other technologies, there's going to be risks.
zh: 第三，如果我们做不好，那么像所有其他技术一样，会有风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the moment you start talking about the singularity and AGI and create this godlike mythology out of AI, you're going to scare a lot of people.
zh: 但当你开始谈论奇点和 AGI，并从 AI 中创造出上帝般的神话时，你会吓到很多人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to be the last remaining private company.
zh: 我们将会成为仅存的私营公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, truly.
zh: 真的，就像。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, well, you flew here on United.
zh: 就像，嗯，你是坐联合航空来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know how that's going to work.
zh: 我不知道那将如何运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, you know, there's going to be a lot of change if people think that there's going to be one company.
zh: 是的，我的意思是，你知道，如果人们认为将会只有一家公司，那将会发生很多变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think Sam Altman just did an interview where, yeah, and kudos to him, it's hard to go back and say I was wrong.
zh: 我认为 Sam Altman 刚刚接受了一次采访，是的，称赞他一下，回过头来承认自己是很难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He basically says, I totally underestimated the momentum of the economy, the momentum of existing businesses, and so I predicted this future that actually has not come true.
zh: 他基本上是说，我完全低估了经济动力，现有业务的动力，所以我预测的这个未来实际上并没有成真。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that that's a great reckoning where you go and you say, I didn't think that this was going to happen and it's clearly not going that way.
zh: 我认为那是一个很好的审视，你会去说，我不认为这会发生，而且显然没有那样发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm revising my prediction.
zh: 所以我正在修正我的预测。

speaker: Unknown
en: What did you not think was going to happen where you had to revise your prediction?
zh: 你不认为会发生什么，以至于你必须修正你的预测？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, I love that question.
zh: 哦，我喜欢这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the biggest thing that surprised me where I've had to go back and seriously correct my priors
zh: 我认为让我感到意外最大的事情是我不得不回去并认真修正我的先验观念

speaker: Unknown
en: is building a business is much more reactive than planning.
zh: 是建立一家公司比规划更具反应性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I mean by that is almost every one of our best decisions as a company has been in reaction to some information and a split-second decision, sort of, rather than a master plan that we forecasted six months ahead.
zh: 我的意思是，几乎我们作为公司做出的每一个最好的决定都是对某些信息和瞬间决定的反应，而不是我们提前六个月预测的总体计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that knowing that, you start to look at the rest of the world.
zh: 而且我认为知道了这一点，你开始看世界其他地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: You hear from other business leaders how that's also how they make decisions.
zh: 你从其他商业领袖那里听到，这也是他们做决定的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you start to realize that the world is just this constantly reactive feedback loop where people are just talking to each other and making decisions, and no one actually has an answer to what the future is going to look like.
zh: 然后你开始意识到，世界只是这样一个不断反应的反馈循环，人们只是互相交谈并做决定，没有人实际上对未来是什么样有答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you basically just start defining it in real time in group chats and in the actions that you take as a business.
zh: 所以你基本上只是开始在群聊和你作为一家公司采取的行动中实时定义它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that learning that in real time has made me totally, one, question the existing world and structure.
zh: 所以我认为实时学到这一点让我完全地，第一，质疑现有的世界和结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, nothing's guaranteed and anything could change.
zh: 基本上，没有任何事情是保证的，任何事都可能改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And two, it's quite empowering.
zh: 第二，这相当让人有力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes you realize you're basically a couple of decisions away from even greater outcomes and even bigger business than you had prior.
zh: 它让你意识到，你基本上离做出几个决定就能获得比以前更大的成果和更大的生意只有几步之遥。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally got that on that anything could change.
zh: 完全理解了任何事都可能改变这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that I hope changes is margins and margin profiles.
zh: 我希望改变的一件事是利润率和利润率特征。

speaker: Unknown
en: Help me understand, when we look across the wave of incredible businesses in AI, the margin profiles are still lower than they were previously, 30% to 35%, say, as a barometer compared to 70%, 80% with SaaS.
zh: 帮我理解一下，当我们纵观 AI 领域令人难以置信的商业浪潮时，利润率特征仍然比以前低，比如说以 30% 到 35% 作为指标，与 SaaS 的 70%、80% 相比。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that a momentary period in time where we're in a build-out phase and they expand over time, or is that just a net new, but the revenues are going to be much larger?
zh: 这是一个暂时的时期，我们处于建设阶段，它们会随时间扩张，还是说这只是全新的东西，但收入会大得多？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, not all businesses in AI have bad margin profiles.
zh: 嗯，并非所有 AI 领域的生意都有糟糕的利润率特征。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I know we've got good margins.
zh: 我的意思是，我知道我们有很好的利润率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that actually comes in a way that I think is also customer aligned in that we are so focused on sort of thinking about these outcomes themselves as the thing to be valued.
zh: 这实际上以一种我认为也与客户一致的方式出现，因为我们要如此专注于思考这些结果本身作为价值所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've kind of gone away from a lot of common paths that we see other AI companies doing.
zh: 所以我们有点偏离了我们看到其他 AI 公司正在做的很多常见路径。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't subsidize consumers in the dev tool space.
zh: 我们不在开发工具领域补贴消费者。

speaker: Unknown
en: That hurts us in a lot of ways.
zh: 这在很多方面伤害了我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have the mind share from self-service users.
zh: 我们没有来自自助服务用户的心智份额。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have no PLG?
zh: 所以你没有产品驱动增长？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would separate self-service from PLG.
zh: 我会把自助服务和产品驱动增长区分开。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a lot of focus on PLG within companies that we've deployed to, to allow the adoption to increase.
zh: 我们非常专注于在我们部署到的公司内部做产品驱动增长，以增加采用率。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what we don't have is a consumer public-facing plan that is, I would say, super rational for a current consumer, unless you're optimizing for quality.
zh: 但我们没有的是，我想说，对于当前的消费者来说超级理性的面向消费者的公开计划，除非你在优化质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Should you?
zh: 你应该吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: In a LangGraph environment like today, should you?
zh: 在像今天这样的 LangGraph 环境中，你应该吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a really good question.
zh: 我认为这是一个非常好的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: In my mind, the biggest reason for this is there are two players with effectively infinite money who are trying to flood the market, and their intent is if we flood the market, we keep you.
zh: 在我看来，最大的原因是有两个拥有实际上无限资金的参与者正在试图充斥市场，他们的意图是如果我们充斥市场，我们就能留住你。

speaker: Unknown
en: But remember what we talked about just a second ago, you don't keep them.
zh: 但记得我们刚才谈论的，你留不住他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: After you sort of pull back the subsidies, as we've learned, I think that probably the consumer will continue to follow the sort of like most cost effective solution.
zh: 在你有点撤回补贴后，据我们所知，我认为消费者可能会继续追随那种最具成本效益的解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what does that look like in one, two, three years?
zh: 那么在一两年或三年后这会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's open models.
zh: 我认为会是开放模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the most cost effective solution for a model is going to be the cheap one that you can run locally on your computer.
zh: 我认为对于模型来说最具成本效益的解决方案将是可以在你计算机上本地运行的廉价模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we want to make sure that we are the product that best fits that type of experience.
zh: 所以我们要确保我们是最适合那种体验的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's why we're so optimized on local and on open models today for on-prem, but in the future it's for all consumers.
zh: 这就是为什么我们今天在本地和开放模型上做了如此多的优化以进行本地部署，但在未来它是为了所有消费者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we won't have to subsidize as much as we'll have to create an amazing experience for self-service.
zh: 所以我们不需要像那样多地去补贴，我们将必须为自助服务创造惊人的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think of this as like a long game where eventually the self-service will come to us, but not because we subsidize, but because we have the best product in market.
zh: 所以我把这看作是一场长期的博弈，最终自助服务会来找我们，不是因为我们补贴，而是因为我们要有市场上最好的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're advising me as an investor, say, on how to think about margin and how that plays into my decision to invest or not in a business, what would you say?
zh: 所以如果你作为投资者给我建议，比如说，关于如何思考利润率以及它如何影响我投资或不投资一家公司的决定，你会说什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that for us, this is a part of our strategy.
zh: 我认为对我们来说，这是我们策略的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't mean though that it's the only way to win.
zh: 但这并不意味着这是获胜的唯一方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think that there's probably going to be businesses where they're able to lock you in because of a workflow or a system of record that they produce and the margins or the subsidies temporarily reducing margin can be a route towards gaining.
zh: 我确实认为可能会有这样的企业，它们因为其产生的工作流或记录系统而能够锁定你，而且利润率或暂时降低利润率的补贴可以是一种获取客户的途径。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a classic strategy, right?
zh: 这是一个经典的策略，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This isn't even new to AI, gaining customer base.
zh: 这对 AI 来说甚至都不新鲜，获取客户群。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I would say, though, is that if there's no path to increasing the margin profile, that is very risky.
zh: 不过我想说的是，如果没有

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that a lot of investments are being made in businesses where the promise is simply that they will raise prices, but you won't see a consummate increase in the value of the platform.
zh: 我认为很多投资正投向那些仅仅是承诺会提高价格，但你不会看到平台价值相应增加的企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is so competitive in AI right now.
zh: 现在的 AI 领域竞争非常激烈。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are not also raising the outcomes and the value that you get out of the product while you raise that price, people will churn and move to another thing.
zh: 如果你在提高价格的同时，没有提高产品带来的结果和价值，人们就会流失并转向别的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do think it's quite tricky and the margin profile actually matters a lot, but it's not end all be all.
zh: 所以我确实认为这很棘手，利润概况实际上很重要，但这并不是一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Will you have that churn in enterprise sales?
zh: 在企业销售中会有那种流失吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You work with some of the biggest companies in the world.
zh: 你与世界上一些最大的公司合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure you sign year long, minimum, multi-year long.
zh: 我确信你签的合同至少一年，通常是多年。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have pretty sticky client bases there, no?
zh: 你在那里的客户基础相当有粘性，不是吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think so.
zh: 我认为如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that people also see these year or multi-year partnerships as just that, like a partnership.
zh: 我认为人们也把这些一年或多年的合作关系仅仅看作是一种合作关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Part of what makes it interesting to build right now is that a lot of what you're selling is not only the technology, but your knowledge about how to best use that technology.
zh: 现在进行构建之所以有趣的部分原因在于，你销售的大部分内容不仅是技术，还有你关于如何最好地使用该技术的知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which I would carefully differentiate from consulting or professional services in that you don't actually have to go in and do all of the implementation or... And I honestly think if you have a product that requires 100 FDEs to get it deployed, you just have a bad product.
zh: 我会小心地将其与咨询或专业服务区分开来，因为你实际上不需要进去做所有的实施工作……而且我诚实地认为，如果你有一个产品需要 100 个 FDE 才能部署，那你只是有一个糟糕的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: But instead, I think that if you have...
zh: 相反，我认为如果你有……

speaker: Unknown
en: The advice and the knowledge of the direction that you think the world should go on, you're selling that with the product.
zh: 关于你认为世界应该朝哪个方向发展的建议和知识，你是连同产品一起出售的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so people are willing to go and buy that.
zh: 所以人们愿意去买单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that if they see it from you today, they sort of know that in a year, you'll also still have that same knowledge and sort of forward thinkingness.
zh: 我认为如果他们今天从你这里看到了这一点，他们有点知道一年后，你仍然会拥有同样的知识和某种前瞻性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, obviously, lots of people can give that.
zh: 当然，显然很多人都能提供这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you combine that with a product that then acts a little bit more as a platform or a system rather than a tool that people use, you can also get stickier by just being something that you build on top of.
zh: 但如果你将其与一个更像平台或系统的产品结合起来，而不是人们使用的工具，你也可以通过成为人们在其上构建的东西而变得更有粘性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We spoke about the different frontier model providers essentially having this really challenging dynamic of being locked into their own models when serving, say, Claude Code or any application that they choose to serve.
zh: 我们谈到了不同的前沿模型提供商本质上面临着这种极具挑战性的动态，即在提供服务时，比如提供 Claude Code 或他们选择服务的任何应用程序，会被锁定在自己的模型中。

speaker: Unknown
en: One then thinks that the value becomes in the routing of models, the task to the model, what's optimized for each use case, cost, latency, function, whatever it is.
zh: 人们就会认为价值在于模型的路由、分配给模型的任务、针对每个用例进行的优化（成本、延迟、功能等）。

speaker: Unknown
en: An open router gets bought for $8 billion.
zh: 一个开放路由器以 80 亿美元的价格被收购。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the values in the routing, great.
zh: 所有的价值都在路由中，很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then everyone is doing routing.
zh: 然后每个人都在做路由。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ramp has a routing provider.
zh: Ramp 有一个路由提供商。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my companies, Merge.dev, has one.
zh: 我的一家公司，Merge.dev，有一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in another startup, Requesty.
zh: 我们涉足另一家初创公司，Requesty。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, well, the routing is completely commoditized.
zh: 我就想，好吧，路由已经完全商品化了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Help me understand, what world do we live in?
zh: 帮我理解一下，我们生活在什么样的世界里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think that routing is a really interesting technology in that I don't think the technology itself is necessarily that differentiated.
zh: 嗯，我认为路由是一项非常有趣的技术，因为我认为该技术本身不一定有那么大的差异化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if somebody comes up and says, look, Stripe bought OpenRouter for $8 billion because of the technology.
zh: 所以如果有人过来说，看，Stripe 因为这项技术花了 80 亿美元买下了 OpenRouter。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I'd say either A, if they have insider knowledge, then that was a bad decision.
zh: 那么我会说，要么 A，如果他们有内部消息，那是一个糟糕的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: If B, they're just sort of assigning that to it, I think they're missing what I read when I read the letter to shareholders, which was that they see this as a bet on where the direction of capital allocation is going.
zh: 如果是 B，他们只是把那个归因于它，我认为他们错过了我读致股东信时读到的内容，即他们把这看作是对资本配置方向去向的押注。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about it like this.
zh: 像这样想。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are tokens other than intelligence?
zh: 除了智能，tokens 还是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do you get tokens?
zh: 你怎么获得 tokens？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you pay for them.
zh: 嗯，你为此付费。

speaker: Unknown
en: How does the infrastructure layer get energy?
zh: 基础设施层如何获得能量？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's literally like translating energy into intelligence, and you're just trading dollars along the way.
zh: 字面上就像把能量转化为智能，你只是在过程中用美元进行交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of this is basically converging towards one thing.
zh: 所有这些基本上都在汇聚向一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether you call it allocating energy, allocating intelligence, allocating money, businesses need to allocate whatever this is in order to grow and expand how they operate and grow and expand their bottom line.
zh: 无论你称之为分配能量、分配智能还是分配金钱，企业都需要分配这其中的任何东西，以便增长和扩展它们的运营方式，并增长和扩展它们的底线。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're Stripe, you already control the flow of one out of the three of these.
zh: 如果你是 Stripe，你已经控制了这三者中之一的流向。

speaker: Unknown
en: With OpenRouter, rather than the routing technology,
zh: 有了 OpenRouter，而不是路由技术，

speaker: Unknown
en: You actually just gain the information of where these models are going, right?
zh: 你实际上只是获得了这些模型去向的信息，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You start to understand what are people doing with intelligence?
zh: 你开始明白人们在用智能做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How are they allocating it?
zh: 他们如何分配它？

speaker: Unknown
en: To what models are they using?
zh: 他们正在使用什么模型？

speaker: Unknown
en: So now you start to control the second of these three things.
zh: 所以现在你开始控制这三件事中的第二件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe they'll make a play into energy infrastructure or data centers at some point.
zh: 也许他们会在某个时候进军能源基础设施或数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: But just ownership over those two is a massive bet on how to think about where companies allocate resources.
zh: 但仅仅拥有这两者就是对如何思考公司资源分配去向的巨大押注。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for them, I think this is very reasonable.
zh: 所以对他们来说，我认为这是非常合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what's interesting is you wouldn't pay $8 billion for the same company that had no users with better technology.
zh: 但有趣的是，你不会花 80 亿美元去买一家没有用户但技术更好的同一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that difference, I think, is really important.
zh: 所以我认为那个区别真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it gets towards that broader idea of the technology is just no longer the moat.
zh: 它触及了那个更宏大的理念，即技术已不再是护城河。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think it was a good buy?
zh: 你认为这是一笔好的收购吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: At $8 billion, it would have to be really foundational to the team that becomes whatever this next bet on allocating capital is for Stripe, or rather helping the businesses that Stripe has as customers allocate capital.
zh: 出价 80 亿美元，它必须对那个团队来说真正具有基础性意义，这个团队成为了 Stripe 下一步关于配置资本的押注，或者说帮助那些作为 Stripe 客户的企业配置资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say that if they think that data gives them insight into how to run Stripe better as well, that could also potentially make it worth it.
zh: 我会说，如果他们认为数据给了他们关于如何更好地运营 Stripe 的洞察，那可能也会让它物有所值。

speaker: Unknown
en: $8 billion is quite steep though.
zh: 不过 80 亿美元是相当昂贵的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stranger things have happened.
zh: 更奇怪的事情也发生过。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like $8 and $10 billion is the new $1 billion.
zh: 感觉 80 亿和 100 亿美元是新的 10 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm intrigued.
